title: Isolate tenant retry circuits and implement priority-aware dequeuing for async workers
creator: Devon Chen
description:
Background:
Redwood's current async pipeline mixes tenant traffic in shared consumer loops and conflates retry accounting across tenants. A single noisy tenant or pathological message shape can exhaust worker concurrency and retry budget, creating cross-tenant latency spikes and SLO violations. Additionally, our dequeue path is FIFO-only which worsens latency for high-priority control plane messages during bursts.

Goals:
- Isolate retry/circuit state per-tenant so failing tenants do not consume global retry budgets or backpressure tokens.
- Introduce a priority-aware dequeue stage so high-priority messages (control plane, canary traffic, small-chat requests) are favored without starving regular traffic.
- Propagate backpressure signals from worker pools up to the ingress routers and client throttlers to avoid unbounded queueing.
- Upgrade kafka-go client to v2.1.0 to gain rebalance and commit performance fixes; ensure compatibility with our consumer-shim.
- Clean up Redis delayed queue TTL handling and remove deprecated Lua scripts to reduce tail latency for delayed retries.

Scope / Non-goals:
- This ticket focuses on runtime-level refactor and infra changes; prompt/LLM model routing changes are out of scope.

Acceptance criteria:
- Per-tenant retry counters and circuit breaker implemented and tested; one tenant causing repeated retries should not increase retry budget usage for others (verified via unit + integration tests).
- Dequeue latency for priority=high messages p99 reduced by >=40% under simulated burst compared to baseline.
- End-to-end p95 latency for normal traffic unchanged +/-5% in steady state.
- Backpressure metrics emitted and visible in Console: tenant.backpressure.active, worker.pool_utilization, ingress.rejected_rate.
- Kafka consumer upgraded and all integration tests pass; documented upgrade notes in Confluence.
- No regressions in message ordering semantics for partitioned topics (smoke tested).

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Use a two-tier queue: a small constant-sized priority ringbuffer (in-memory) for high-priority requests and a general consumer queue for bulk traffic. This avoids heap allocations and keeps fast-path hot.
- Retry bookkeeping will be sharded by tenant-id in an embedded in-memory store persisted to Redis for cross-worker visibility; we accept slightly increased Redis ops for isolation vs a fully local-only store.
- Backpressure tokens are emitted as tracing metrics and as a short-lived lease in Redis. Ingress will subscribe to token shortage TTLs to decide to shed or route to Dedicated.
- Kafka client upgrade chosen for rebalance stability and improved commit batching; requires minor consumer-shim changes (see notes).

Implementation plan / milestones:
- Spike (2 days): prototype priority ringbuffer and per-tenant retry counter APIs. Benchmark with synthetic workload. (Devon)
- Refactor consumer loop (4 days): split dequeue => priority fetch => commit flow, add per-tenant circuit interface. (Ava + Rahul)
- Redis work (2 days): migrate TTL-based delayed retry to new key schema and remove old Lua scripts; add small script for atomic token set. (Priya)
- Kafka upgrade (3 days): upgrade client, adjust rebalance handlers, run integration tests in staging. (Sven)
- Testing & rollout (4 days): unit tests, integration tests with staging traffic replay, gradual canary rollout with feature flag. Monitor metrics and rollback plan. (team)
risk_and_mitigation:
Risks:
- Rebalance regressions after kafka client upgrade could cause duplicate processing. Mitigation: run extended consumer tests with long-lived groups, enable idempotent commit path, and ship behind a feature flag.
- Incorrect per-tenant sharding might increase Redis hot keys. Mitigation: use tenant hashing with jitter and monitor redis.hits_by_key; add fallback to local cache for noisy tenants.
- Priority ringbuffer overflow could drop high-priority messages. Mitigation: fixed-size ring tuned by capacity tests and an emergency overflow path that writes to a reserved partition with TTL.
- Observability gaps during rollout. Mitigation: add dashboard and alert runbook before canary.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for retry counter semantics and circuit open/close transitions.
- Integration tests: stage consumer group replay with mixed tenant traffic and assert per-tenant isolation.
- Load test: burst scenarios with 10x traffic to validate priority dequeue p99 improvement and global p95 stability.
- Chaos test: simulate Kafka rebalance mid-burst, ensure at-most-once-to-at-least-once invariant as documented.
- Staging canary: 5% traffic for 24h, increase to 25% for 48h, monitor latency, errors, redis ops.
rollout_plan:
- Feature-flag gate for priority dequeue and tenant-circuits; default off.
- Deploy kafka client upgrade to a single consumer shard in staging and run 72h.
- Enable per-tenant retry isolation in staging, run traffic replay and measure metrics.
- Canary in prod: enable for internal tenants only (scheduling control plane), monitor dashboard for 6h, then ramp to 10% and 50% over 2 days.
- Full enable only after 7-day post-canary health check and sign-off.
migration_notes:
- New Redis keys: 'tenant:retry:v2:<tenant_id>' and 'backpressure:lease:<pool_id>'. Run a one-time TTL cleanup script during migration window.
- Consumer groups: update group naming convention to include runtime-major to avoid cross-version rebalances.
- Keep old Lua scripts available as read-only fallback for 48h after deploy; remove in next maintenance window.
monitoring_and_alerts:
Dashboards to add/update:
- Console: tenant.retry.circuit_open_count (by tenant), priority.dequeue.latency p50/p95/p99, ingress.shed_rate.
- Pager alerts: if priority.dequeue.p99 > baseline + 100ms for 15m OR worker.pool_utilization > 85% for 10m.
- Silent alert for redis.hot_keys_count > threshold.
